name: Harvey
tagline: Legal AI: an LLM platform for law firms and in-house legal teams (drafting, research, document review, a document Vault). The loop is a recruiter call and hiring-manager screen, a ~60 min technical screen with one multi-part practical coding problem in Python, then a virtual onsite with 1-2 more coding rounds, an LLM/RAG system design round, a project deep dive and a behavioral/values round.
notes: Harvey's coding questions are practical, multi-part and lean on strings, intervals and small stateful designs rather than puzzle algorithms. Most reported for SWE (2025-2026): source/citation highlighting (find every exact occurrence of a set of source strings in an LLM answer, wrap them in tags, merge overlapping or touching spans, count occurrences, then attach the distinct sources cited per region), a spreadsheet with formula cells, eager recomputation and cycle-rejecting writes (reported many times), an in-memory file system / document vault that creates missing directories and gives duplicate files the smallest free '(k)' suffix, and an onsite notebook exercise on embedding retrieval with cosine similarity evaluated with Recall@10 and MRR@10. Also reported: a cursor-based text editor, a duplicate-file finder that handles symlink cycles, and a database connection pool. Candidates say the problems are not individually hard but come with several follow-ups, so speed matters; interviewers want you to pin down edge cases (overlap vs touch, empty inputs, ties, invalid paths) before coding, keep mutations atomic, and talk through complexity.
